q1: SELECT * FROM R1 AS X, (SELECT * FROM R2 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM R3) AS Y
q2: SELECT * FROM R1 AS X, R2 AS Y UNION ALL SELECT * FROM R1 AS X, R3 AS Y
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT * FROM R1 AS X, (SELECT * FROM R2 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM R3) AS Y
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT * FROM R1 AS X, R2 AS Y UNION ALL SELECT * FROM R1 AS X, R3 AS Y
counterexample: INSERT INTO R1 (X) VALUES (1); INSERT INTO R2 (X) VALUES (2); INSERT INTO R3 (X) VALUES (3);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 performs a Cartesian product between R1 and the union of R2 and R3, while Q2 first performs Cartesian products between R1 and R2 and R1 and R3, and then unions the results.
counterexample_dsp: When R1, R2, and R3 all contain at least one row, the results of Q1 and Q2 will differ.
